ai.title: Lite mode fallback to Fireworks standard API
ai.summary: Lite cost mode now routes to Fireworks standard API instead of erroring or using custom deployments. `createFireworksRequestWithFallback` checks `cost_mode === 'lite'` to bypass deployment hours, cooldowns, and 5xx errors. Scope limited to `web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts`.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant with lite cost mode, your requests now go through the standard Fireworks API pathway instead of erroring out or relying on custom model deployments. Previously, lite users who encountered deployment hour limits, cooldown periods, or 5xx server errors would get blocked; now the system automatically falls back to the standard API when you're on the lite plan. You wouldn't see this switching happen, but if you're using lite mode and the custom deployment is unavailable, your request will still complete instead of failing with an error. This applies only to web users who have lite cost mode enabled.

ai.title: Show local freebuff model availability
ai.summary: CLI model selector now displays dynamic deployment availability labels based on user's local timezone. Replaced static `FREEBUFF_DEPLOYMENT_HOURS_LABEL` with `getFreebuffDeploymentAvailabilityLabel()` in `freebuff-model-selector.tsx`. Added timezone-aware date calculation utilities in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` to compute local availability windows. Covers CLI interface; server-facing fallback label remains for API errors.

eli5.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI, it now tells you in plain language whether the free 'buff' model is reachable from your own clock right now, for example, something like 'available until 5pm in your local time' instead of a fixed Eastern/Pacific window. The CLI now looks at the computer's current time and timezone to figure out your local availability window, while servers that can't see your timezone still fall back to the generic Eastern-to-Pacific label. You'd notice this the next time you browse models in the CLI picker; it's the kind of change you'd only see if you were actively picking a model, and it only helps when the live availability data is actually flowing through, not when an API error forces the stale fallback text.

ai.title: Raise MiniMax instant admit threshold
ai.summary: MiniMax instant admit capacity increased from 200 to 1000 in `web/src/server/free-session/config.ts`. Change supports higher concurrent usage without altering session grace logic. Scope limited to server config.

eli5.text: When you start using the MiniMax model through the free session system, the server can now let in far more people at the same time before making anyone wait. The limit that decides how many get in immediately was raised from 200 to 1000, so heavy bursts of usage won't trigger the waiting line as quickly. This only affects how the free session system handles MiniMax and does not change how long your session lasts once you're in. The change is live in the server configuration.

ai.title: Fix CLI model picker Enter and navigation logic
ai.summary: Refactored `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` to use new `freebuff-model-navigation.ts` utilities for handling Enter/Space commits and arrow navigation. This ensures the picker correctly resolves the target model ID, prioritizing the focused item if available, otherwise falling back to the selected item, while gracefully handling scenarios where no models are selectable. Updated `use-freebuff-session.ts` to prevent race conditions during restarts by tracking generation IDs and resetting the fetch method to GET for landing states. Adjusted `waiting-room-screen.tsx` to display errors even when a session exists but has a 'none' status.

eli5.text: When you press Enter in the model picker, the CLI now correctly picks the model your keyboard is focused on (instead of falling back to a stale or unavailable selection), and arrow keys wrap around to the same selectable model when all peers are unavailable. This affects anyone using the CLI's Freebuff model selection screen. If you looked, you'd notice the picker reliably resolves to a valid model even in edge cases, and error messages in the waiting room now appear even when a session exists with a 'none' status.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.49 released
ai.summary: Freebuff version bumped from 0.0.48 to 0.0.49 in the CLI release package manifest (`freebuff/cli/release/package.json`). This is a release-bump commit with no functional code changes, bundling previously landed features: Lite mode fallback to the Fireworks standard API, timezone-aware local deployment availability labels in the CLI model selector, MiniMax instant admit threshold raised to 1000, and CLI model picker Enter/navigation fixes using `freebuff-model-navigation.ts`. Users receive these as the consolidated 0.0.49 release.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies only `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `"0.0.48"` to `"0.0.49"` (commit cd5d1d29, Date: 2026-04-25T06:53:56Z). No source code, configuration, or dependency changes are present in this commit.

eli5.text: This release makes the model picker smarter and more reliable while expanding capacity for concurrent users. When you are working in the budget-friendly "lite" cost mode, it now automatically falls back to the standard Fireworks API instead of erroring out or requiring a custom setup, so you always get a working connection. The model selector now shows real-time availability labels based on your local time zone, so you can see at a glance whether a free model is currently available to run in your area. The MiniMax model tier now supports up to 1,000 simultaneous users instead of 200, reducing wait times and improving access during busy periods. Additionally, the keyboard navigation and Enter-key behavior in the model picker have been fixed, so selecting a model with your arrow keys or pressing Enter consistently picks the correct model and avoids confusing race conditions when restarting sessions. For users, this means a smoother daily experience with fewer errors, clearer availability information, better handling of high-traffic moments, and more dependable selection of AI models directly from the command-line interface.

ai.title: ChoiceAdBanner shows ad title when URL missing
ai.summary: The CLI ad banner now displays the ad title instead of a blank space if the ad response lacks a URL. A new `getAdDisplayLabel` helper resolves this fallback, using `extractDomain` for URLs or the title for missing links. The component applies `TextAttributes.DIM` for title fallbacks and truncates text to fit column widths. This change affects `cli/src/components/choice-ad-banner.tsx`.

eli5.text: When an advertisement shown in the command-line tool doesn't include a link, the ad banner now displays the ad's title text instead of leaving that spot blank. You'd notice the banner staying populated with the ad's name rather than going empty when no destination URL is provided. Behind the scenes, a helper picks the title as a fallback whenever the URL is missing, so the banner keeps looking consistent.

ai.title: ChoiceAdBanner label styling tweak
ai.summary: Updated `ChoiceAdBanner` in `cli/src/components/choice-ad-banner.tsx` to use `TextAttributes.BOLD` instead of `DIM` for non-domain labels. Also corrected closing tag syntax.

eli5.text: Small print next to ads now appears in bold instead of a faded style when the ad doesn't include a website link. This only affects the brief labels you might see in the command-line tool. Nothing else changed - the layout and content of the ad banner look the same.

ai.title: Fireworks deployment hours daily
ai.summary: Fireworks deployment availability logic updated to run daily instead of weekdays only. `isFreebuffDeploymentHours` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` removes weekend checks and adjusts `getNextFreebuffDeploymentStart` offset calculation. `FREEBUFF_DEPLOYMENT_HOURS_LABEL` updated to '9am ET-5pm PT every day'. Local time formatting in `getFreebuffDeploymentAvailabilityLabel` drops the 'local' suffix.

eli5.text: The assistant is now available to help during deployment hours every day instead of only on weekdays. You'll see the schedule now says '9am ET-5pm PT every day' and the time shown is in your local time. This is live today, so if you previously couldn't access the assistant on weekend mornings or afternoons, you can now do so during those hours.

ai.title: CanopyWave test scripts add model argument and kimi alias
ai.summary: scripts/test-canopywave-long.ts now accepts a model argument, defaulting to minimax/minimax-m2.5 but supporting moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 via MODEL_CONFIGS and MODEL_ALIASES. MAX_TOKENS increased to 10000 to accommodate reasoning models. scripts/test-canopywave.ts hardcoded model switched to moonshotai/kimi-k2.6. Pricing constants moved into a typed ModelConfig object; unknown models exit with error.

eli5.text: The assistant you chat with can now switch between two different AI models during internal testing, instead of being locked to one. When testers run the long-running CanopyWave test, they can choose either the default MiniMax model or the kimi model by typing a simple word, and the system will use the right pricing rates for whichever they pick. If someone tries to use a model the system doesn’t know, it will stop and tell them rather than guessing. One of the test scripts is now also set to use the kimi model by default, which can use more of your tokens when it thinks through answers.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.50
ai.summary: The CLI package manifest at `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` increments its `version` field from 0.0.49 to 0.0.50, continuing the same-day same-component release sequence (0.0.49 was bumped earlier in commit cd5d1d29). This release packages the user-visible CLI improvements shipped earlier today: ChoiceAdBanner now falls back to displaying the ad title when no URL is present, Fireworks free-model deployment hours now run daily instead of weekdays-only, and CanopyWave test scripts accept a model argument and a kimi alias with reasoning-model token headroom.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.49` to `0.0.50`, matching the release-bump commit metadata dated 2026-04-25. This single-line bump is the only change in the package manifest.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI is now at version 0.0.50 with improved ad displays, more reliable model availability, and better test script flexibility. When you see a sponsored ad in the Freebuff CLI that doesn't include a link, it now shows the ad's title text instead of leaving a blank space, so you always get useful information. The styling for these ad labels has also been adjusted for better readability. The Fireworksh-powered models are now available during deployment hours every single day, including weekends, rather than only on weekdays. This means you can access these powerful models for longer and more consistent use. Upgrading to this version gives you a smoother experience with clearer ad information when links are missing, and more dependable access to Fireworksh models throughout the entire week instead of just weekdays. You'll also notice that ads display cleaner formatting with better text styling. These changes improve your daily workflow by ensuring you always see meaningful content in ad banners and can rely on model availability across all days, making your development sessions more productive and less interrupted.

ai.title: Add waiting room ad surface to Gravity
ai.summary: Introduces `waiting_room` ad surface to `useGravityAd` and `Gravity` provider. Maps this surface to specific `waiting-room-*` placement IDs, forcing `choice` variant. Updates `AdProvider` types and `postAds` validation to support the new surface.

eli5.text: When you open the app and are placed in the waiting room, the screen shown while you wait for your turn, the app now requests a different kind of ad to display there. The system tells the ad service that this is the waiting-room screen, and the service responds with ads specifically chosen for that spot. The ad shown will look the same interactive style already used in choice-based ads, just pulled from waiting-room-specific placements. This is live today for anyone who sees the waiting room screen.

ai.title: Route Kimi K2.6 through CanopyWave
ai.summary: Kimi K2.6 requests now route to CanopyWave in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts. CANOPYWAVE_MODELS in web/src/llm-api/canopywave.ts consolidates routing and per-model pricing, replacing hardcoded constants. Pricing updated to $0.95/$0.16/$4.00 per million tokens.

eli5.text: The assistant can now route requests for the Kimi K2.6 model through CanopyWave, a service that handles pricing and model access. Previously, this model was not available through CanopyWave, but the update adds it alongside pricing details ($0.95 per million input tokens, $0.16 for cached input, and $4.00 per million output tokens). You would notice this change if you tried to use the Kimi K2.6 model and expected it to work through CanopyWave, because now it does instead of falling back to other routing.
